parallel.requirements: Recognized the Rust 2021, CLI, byte-exact output, zero-dependency, black-box, complete Cargo project, and standalone test14.rs requirements, including C++ argv and std::stoi edge cases.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Delegated recon, three designs, three judges, and a final spec synthesis through one 10-child workflow while the parent retained implementation tasks and local build/test todo items.
parallel.implementation: The parent wrote multiple tsl and cpp modules plus test14.rs, making a genuine hopscotch-style implementation attempt while design and judge children were still running.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The delivered artifact had Rust source files but no recorded Cargo.toml or built executable in the artifact list, and the final response file was empty.
parallel.verification: The parent probed the C++ binary and prepared a differential harness, but no completed Cargo build, rustc build, cargo test, or differential pass is visible before timeout.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The workflow was killed with spec synthesis in progress, the agent process returned 143 at the timeout, and the official evaluator completed with 0 of 35 tests passed.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same source behavior, CLI/default count rules, std::stoi abort behavior, zero-dependency requirement, Cargo packaging, and standalone entry-file delivery.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Kept ownership in the main serial agent: probe behavior, implement modules, repair discovered issues, build, test, differential-check, and deliver.
serial.implementation: Wrote a Cargo package with test14.rs, tsl hopscotch_hash and hopscotch_map modules, cxx string/terminate shims, tests, README, and a compiled executable.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Integrated the files into a coherent /output project, verified Cargo.lock had only the local package, produced /output/test14, and documented the delivered project.
serial.verification: Ran cargo build --release, cargo test --release, rustc -O --edition 2021, byte-exact differential checks, performance probes, clean rebuild warning checks, and final differential verification.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished task work is evident at closure; clippy was unavailable, but the run handled that as non-blocking after other acceptance checks passed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run recognized the full porting task, including byte-exact CLI/std::stoi behavior and the complete /output project requirement.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run recognized the same task requirements and treated error paths, zero dependencies, standalone rustc, and Cargo packaging as required.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement understanding was broadly similar; the material difference was that serial converted the requirements into verified delivery, while parallel left delivery and validation unfinished.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed into a background workflow with recon, design, judge, and spec children while the parent also created local implementation, build/test, and review todos.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept one owner for probing, implementation, repair, build, differential testing, and final delivery.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent substantial budget coordinating a large planning workflow before the parent completed acceptance work; serial avoided the extra ownership layer and executed the pipeline directly.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel supplied rich shared context to children, including reference behavior and module constraints, but the workflow result was not completed and some children observed in-flight /output state.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial carried the discovered task context locally from probes into code edits and verification without cross-agent handoff loss.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No decisive missing child brief is evidenced; the practical interface difference is that serial's context stayed immediately actionable, while parallel's workflow outputs remained separate from final validation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote hopscotch hash, bucket, iterator, map facade, cpp argv/stoi/terminate modules, and test14.rs, but stopped before confirmed compilation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote analogous hopscotch and C++ shim modules, corrected an insertion relocation issue, and produced a compiled binary.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implemented a substantial from-scratch map, but serial closed the implementation loop with repairs and executable generation; parallel left its source uncompiled and officially failed all tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The workflow had completed recon, design, and judge child results but was killed before the spec child returned; the parent had no final response.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child results to retrieve and ended with a final response summarizing implementation and verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's planned synthesis result never reached a usable completed state, while serial delivered a closed single-agent result lifecycle.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent wrote implementation files while workflow children were reading /output and incorporating the in-flight tree into design judgments, but no concrete overwrite by a child is proven.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial created directories and wrote files in one control flow, then listed the final artifact tree after verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had shared-state exposure between parent-written in-progress files and child planning, while serial's implementation state had one writer and clear provenance.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel probed the reference binary and prepared a harness, but no visible acceptance run completed before timeout and final.txt is empty.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed cargo build, cargo test, rustc build, differential tests, byte comparisons, and clean rebuild warning checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the clearest delivery difference: serial verified before closure and passed, while parallel exhausted the run before the planned build/test stage.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used a long 10-child workflow, 660450 workflow child tokens, timed out at the agent budget, and still had the spec child in progress.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed in 780.699 agent seconds, with no subagents and remaining provider budget, then passed official evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel run's fan-out consumed the closure window; serial preserved enough budget to build, test, and finalize.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official records make this a serial_only_pass pair: parallel failed 0/35 and serial passed 35/35. The concrete task-solving difference is closure and acceptance, not initial understanding. Parallel launched and maintained a large design workflow, wrote source while the workflow was live, and then timed out with the workflow killed, final spec still in progress, no final response, and no observed build/test loop. Serial implemented comparable functionality in one flow, corrected issues, built with Cargo and rustc, ran differential checks, checked clean rebuild diagnostics, and delivered a complete artifact that passed all official tests.
parallel_contributors: The 10-child workflow consumed most of the finite run and ended killed before spec synthesis, build, differential testing, and finalization completed.
The parallel artifact list lacks the Cargo.toml and compiled executable outputs that the serial artifact contains, and the final response is empty.
serial_contributors: Serial kept implementation, repair, build, and differential testing in one control flow.
Serial executed cargo build, cargo test, rustc, byte-level differential checks, and clean rebuild checks before final delivery.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The available records do not expose the evaluator's exact compile/runtime error for the parallel artifact, so source-level defects separate from timeout are not asserted as the unique cause.
Serial included memory and README writes outside the core evaluator path; those do not explain the pass/fail difference.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an exclusive root cause

candidates.reason: The parent was an active implementation owner and wrote the Rust modules and test14.rs; the problem was unfinished validation under timeout, not absent implementation ownership.
There were not separately owned component implementations that lacked a reconciler; the children mainly produced recon/design/judgment reports while the parent wrote the code.
The parent had the deliverable responsibility and created entry/source files; missing final package closure is better captured by the budget-exhausted workflow chain.
The parent explicitly tracked implementation, build/test, and review tasks, so there was a pipeline owner even though that owner exhausted the budget before finishing.
The workflow was a large parallel recon/design mechanism, not one mandatory serial preflight; the parent began implementation while it was still running.
Investigation and design children did run before later phases, but parent implementation overlapped with the workflow; the retained issue is collective fan-out exhausting the budget.
The evidence shows broad fan-out consuming the finite run, not merely auxiliary workers starving one critical implementation path.

The parent launched a ten-child recon/design/judge/spec workflow, the workflow ran for roughly 31 minutes with 660450 child tokens and was killed, and the parent timed out before build/test/finalization while serial completed those stages.
candidates.realized_consequence: Build, differential testing, clean rebuild verification, final response, and complete packaging were displaced before timeout; the official parallel solution failed 0/35 while serial passed.
candidates.near_match_reason: The spec child was still in progress when the workflow was killed, but that cancellation is the downstream terminal state of the same broad fan-out budget-exhaustion episode.

candidates.reason: The unfinished spec child was broad, but the budget loss came from the whole 10-child multi-phase workflow, not one isolated oversized child scope.

Children were not delegated separately owned implementation components expected to interoperate; they returned analysis and design reports, so no cross-agent component contract incompatibility is proven.
No known finding is shown being omitted or truncated during transfer and then causing repeated work; the workflow outputs were mostly present but not completed as a whole.
The child handoffs were large, but the parent did not face a visible decision where present bulk information could not be reduced; the run timed out with the workflow killed.
Some children saw in-flight output state, but no receiver is shown acting on a superseded handoff to create an invalid implementation or verification step.
Different design preferences existed, but no incompatible returned contracts remained unadjudicated at an integration decision that caused a concrete mismatch.
The parallel final response is empty and no observable parent acceptance decision presents the whole task as complete; this is an unfinished closure, not unsupported completion.
There is no replacement or retry child that repeats prior work without inherited checkpoints; provider retry was not used.

The parent did not merely wait blindly until timeout; it inspected progress and wrote implementation files, so the more specific issue is the broad fan-out consuming closure budget.

Although workflow children observed /output while the parent wrote files, multiple live agents writing the shared implementation workspace and causing unstable provenance is not proven.
